Hermitian matrix model (Z=∫dMe−S(M))

Words: 179 Articles: 2
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A Hermitian matrix model replaces a spacetime field by a finite-dimensional Hermitian matrix. Its normalized integral supplies correlation functions and a zero-dimensional perturbative quantum field theory expansion. For an action built from traces of matrix powers, unitary matrix conjugation is a symmetry and the eigenvalues describe the invariant degrees of freedom. A quartic real integral needs a nonnegative highest-order coupling for convergence; a formal power series can be studied independently of this convergence issue.

Matrix diagonalization ghost determinant (det′addiagλ​∝∏i<j​(λi​−λj​)2)

Words: 64
Hermitian matrix model OurBigBook.com
Imposing vanishing off-diagonal entries with auxiliary integrations and an off-diagonal Grassmann Gaussian integral gives a determinant of the commutator map on the off-diagonal matrix units. Its eigenvalues are λi​−λj​, i=j. Up to a constant sign, their product is the squared Vandermonde determinant. It contributes −2∑i<j​log∣λi​−λj​∣ to the eigenvalue action, encoding repulsion between distinct eigenvalues. Diagonal zero modes and constant normalization factors must be treated separately.

Quartic Hermitian matrix two-point function (⟨Mij​Mkl​⟩c​)

Words: 53
Hermitian matrix model OurBigBook.com
For S=atr(M2)/2+btr(M4)/4 with a>0, the Wick theorem gives
⟨Mij​Mkl​⟩c​=a1​δil​δkj​−a3b​(2Nδil​δkj​+δij​δkl​)+O(b2).
(1)
There are eight adjacent external-attachment contractions with one free matrix-index sum and four opposite attachments with no free sum. The second tensor structure is needed at finite N; omitting it is an additional large-N approximation, not merely restricting to connected Feynman diagrams.

Radiative correction

Words: 34
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A radiative correction is a quantum correction beyond the classical or tree approximation, represented in perturbative quantum field theory by Feynman diagrams of positive loop order. Such corrections can alter a scalar potential and its derivatives; symmetries and renormalization constrain which changes are allowed.

Perturbation series

Words: 69 Articles: 1
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A perturbation series expands a correlation function or scattering amplitude in powers of interaction couplings. In quantum field theory it is commonly asymptotic because diagram counts grow factorially and nonperturbative effects are invisible to every finite order.

Weak coupling

Words: 32
Perturbation series OurBigBook.com
Weak coupling means a suitably dimensionless interaction strength is small. In BCS theory, νs​V≪1 gives a gap exponentially small compared with the pairing-shell energy cutoff; the expansion parameter is not the dimensional quantity V alone.

Differentiation of the Dyson time-ordered exponential (i∂t​U=HI​(t)U)

Words: 84
Dyson series OurBigBook.com
For bounded norm-continuous Hamiltonian operators on [t0​,t], the Dyson series has an n-th term bounded by Mn∣t−t0​∣n/n!, so it converges in operator norm. In its nested-integral form, differentiating the outer endpoint puts HI​(t) on the left of the (n−1)-fold term. Summing yields ∂t​U=−iHI​(t)U and U(t0​,t0​)=I. If HI​ is Hermitian, differentiating U†U proves unitarity. For unbounded field operators the same algebra is a formal perturbative identity unless domain and convergence assumptions or a regulator justify the steps. Evolution backward uses inverse, anti-time-ordered evolution.

Wick's theorem

Words: 714 Articles: 14
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Wick theorem expresses a time-ordered product of free fields as its normal-ordered product plus the sum over every possible contraction. It turns the Dyson series into Feynman diagrams.

Two-field Wick contraction identity (Tϕ(x)ϕ(y)=:ϕ(x)ϕ(y):+DF​(x−y))

Words: 53
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
Split a free scalar field into its annihilation and creation parts. For x0>y0, changing the product into normal ordering adds [ϕ(+)(x),ϕ(−)(y)], the positive-frequency two-point function. For the opposite ordering interchange the two points. Their combination is the Feynman propagator, equal to the vacuum expectation of the time-ordered product. Iterating this identity gives the scalar Wick theorem.

Two-field scalar Wick identity (T{ϕ(x)ϕ(y)}=:ϕ(x)ϕ(y):+ΔF​(x−y)1)

Words: 47
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
For a free real scalar field, split ϕ=ϕ(+)+ϕ(−) into annihilation and creation parts. Moving the creation operators left gives ϕ(x)ϕ(y)=:ϕ(x)ϕ(y):+[ϕ(+)(x),ϕ(−)(y)]. The commutator is the Wightman function. Choosing either time order gives the displayed identity with the Feynman propagator. It is an identity of operator-valued distributions; coincident-point products need a suitable prescription.

Inductive proof of the scalar Wick theorem

Words: 125
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
Split each free real scalar field as ϕ=ϕ(−)+ϕ(+), into creation and annihilation parts. For chronologically ordered arguments, the first field has the latest time. Multiplying it into a normal-ordered product of the remaining fields gives
ϕ1​:∏r∈I​ϕr​:=:ϕ1​∏r∈I​ϕr​:+∑j∈I​[ϕ1(+)​,ϕj(−)​]:∏r∈I∖{j}​ϕr​:.
(3)
This follows by commuting the annihilation part through each creation part; each commutator is a scalar, and all creation parts commute among themselves, as do all annihilation parts. The scalar commutator is the Feynman propagator for the chronological pair. Induction on the number of fields therefore lists every partial pairing exactly once: either field 1 remains unpaired or it pairs with one j. This proves the Wick theorem for free bosonic fields, including the empty pairing. Vacuum expectation retains only complete pairings. The identities are understood for regulated or smeared operator-valued distributions.

Free scalar four-point function (⟨Tϕ1​ϕ2​ϕ3​ϕ4​⟩)

Words: 44
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
For a centered free real scalar field, its vacuum time-ordered product has expectation ⟨Tϕ1​ϕ2​ϕ3​ϕ4​⟩=G12​G34​+G13​G24​+G14​G23​, where Gij​ is the Feynman propagator between insertions i,j. These are the three complete pairings in the Wick theorem. All remaining normal-ordered products have zero vacuum expectation. No fermionic interchange signs occur for a bosonic field.

Vanishing odd correlators of a free Gaussian field (⟨f​1​⋯f​2n+1​⟩=0)

Words: 55
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
A centered free field in a Gaussian vacuum has only pair contractions, so every odd correlator vanishes by Wick theorem. Equivalently, number parity reverses the field while preserving the vacuum. This statement applies to smeared or regulated fields; it does not assert that unregulated coincident products exist. Interactions or a nonzero field mean can invalidate it.

Time ordering

Words: 219 Articles: 4
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
Time ordering places operators with later time arguments to the left. Interchanging fermionic operators also contributes the sign of the required permutation.

Time-ordered exponential (U(t,t0​)=Texp[−i∫t0​t​H(s)ds/ℏ])

Words: 158 Articles: 2
Time ordering OurBigBook.com
The time-ordered exponential solves iℏ∂t​U=H(t)U with initial condition U(t0​,t0​)=I. Its expansion is the Dyson series. For bounded continuous Hamiltonian operators the series converges, as in differentiation of the Dyson time-ordered exponential. If the generators commute at all times, time ordering is unnecessary and an ordinary operator exponential suffices.
Magnus expansion (U(T)=exp(Ω1​+Ω2​+⋯))
Words: 73
Time-ordered exponential OurBigBook.com
For U˙=A(t)U and U(0)=I, the Magnus expansion writes the logarithm of the propagator as iterated integrals of commutators. Its first terms are Ω1​=∫0T​A(t)dt and Ω2​=21​∫0T​dt∫0t​ds[A(t),A(s)]. For a Quantum Hamiltonian, A=−iH/ℏ, so a noncommuting time-dependent control has corrections beyond the exponential of its integrated Quantum Hamiltonian. This formula is a local convergent expansion under suitable smallness conditions, or a formal expansion; it must not be assumed globally convergent for arbitrary pulse durations.
Constant pulse-axis condition for removing time ordering ([H(t),H(s)]=0⟹U(T)=e−i∫0T​H(t)dt/ℏ)
Words: 44
Time-ordered exponential OurBigBook.com
For H(t)=Ω1​(t)A+Ω2​(t)B with fixed noncommuting Hermitian operators, [H(t),H(s)]=[Ω1​(t)Ω2​(s)−Ω2​(t)Ω1​(s)][A,B]. A constant ratio of the envelopes is sufficient to remove time ordering. Independently changing that ratio generally produces commutator corrections in the Magnus expansion, and a product of successive pulses need not equal the exponential of their summed areas.

Time-ordered product (T{O1​⋯On​})

Words: 39
Time ordering OurBigBook.com
A time-ordered product sorts operator insertions from latest time on the left to earliest time on the right. Reordering odd fermionic operators contributes the sign of their permutation. For bosonic A,B, T[A(t)B(t′)]=θ(t−t′)A(t)B(t′)+θ(t′−t)B(t′)A(t). Vacuum expectations of free time-ordered products are evaluated by the Wick theorem.

Normal ordering

Words: 115 Articles: 2
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
Normal ordering places creation operators to the left of annihilation operators. For free fields it removes vacuum self-contractions from a composite operator.

Normal and Weyl symbols of a harmonic oscillator

Words: 54
Normal ordering OurBigBook.com
For the quantum harmonic oscillator H=ℏω(a†a+1/2), its normal symbol is HN​=ℏω(ψˉ​ψ+1/2). The Weyl ordering symbol of a†a is ψˉ​ψ−1/2, so HW​=ℏωψˉ​ψ=p2/(2m)+mω2q2/2. Switching from adjacent-label coherent-state time slicing to a midpoint phase-space path integral must retain this ordering correction. Both correctly normalized constructions give the thermal partition function of a quantum harmonic oscillator Z=[2sinh(βℏω/2)]−1; retaining the normal-symbol constant after switching prescriptions would count the zero-point shift twice.

Normal-ordered product (:O1​⋯On​:)

Words: 39
Normal ordering OurBigBook.com
A normal-ordered product of free-field oscillator operators places all creation operators to the left of all annihilation operators, including the fermionic sign required to reorder fermions. Its vacuum expectation vanishes if any nontrivial oscillator factors remain. The Wick theorem expresses a free-field time-ordered product through these products and all Wick contractions.

Wick contraction

Words: 31
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
A Wick contraction replaces a selected pair of free fields by their two-point function. Summing pairings computes Gaussian correlation functions and supplies the propagator lines and combinatorial factors of a Feynman diagram.

Fermionic sign

Words: 107 Articles: 1
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A fermionic sign is a factor −1 produced whenever two Grassmann-odd fields or fermionic creation and annihilation operators are interchanged. Relative signs between diagrams must be computed after putting every external fermion operator into one common order.

Antifermion sign of a normal-ordered bilinear (:ψˉ​Γψ:⊃−d†dvˉΓv)

Words: 70
Fermionic sign OurBigBook.com
In a Dirac field mode expansion, the antiparticle contribution to ψˉ​Γψ first appears with operator order dd†. Normal ordering changes it to −d†d using the fermionic anticommutation relations. Thus its scattering coefficient is −vˉin​Γvout​. Pair-annihilation and creation terms have the operator orders db and b†d†. Keeping these orders and a fixed external-state convention determines interference signs, especially between exchange and annihilation graphs in a Yukawa interaction.

Wick rotation

Words: 77 Articles: 1
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A Wick rotation deforms a time or energy contour from real to imaginary values, converting suitable Minkowski integrals into Euclidean integrals while respecting pole prescriptions.

Euclidean action (SE​)

Words: 52
Wick rotation OurBigBook.com
A Wick rotation from real time to imaginary time replaces the oscillatory weight eiS by e−SE​. For a real scalar with positive kinetic normalization, SE​=∫[21​(∂ϕ)2+V(ϕ)]ddx. Positivity of its kinetic term does not ensure convergence if the potential is unbounded below. Fermionic integrals instead use independent Grassmann fields and need not define a positive measure.

Generating functional (Z[J])

Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A generating functional is a path integral with a source J coupled to a field. Its functional derivatives with respect to J generate time-ordered correlation functions.

Polynomial interactions as source differential operators (Z[J]=exp(i∫LI​[i1​δJδ​])Z0​[J])

Words: 70
Generating functional OurBigBook.com
In a finite-dimensional integral, ui​eb⋅u=∂bi​​eb⋅u. Expand eV(u) as a formal perturbation series to obtain ∫due−uTAu/2+b⋅u+V(u)=eV(∂b​)I0​(b). With a finite-mode regulator, a Minkowski source insertion satisfies ϕ(x)ei∫Jϕ=(1/i)δei∫Jϕ/δJ(x); this gives the displayed interacting generating functional. The substitution is a perturbative differential-operator identity, not an assertion that the interaction exponential defines a convergent series. Divide the resulting functional by Z[0] for normalized correlation functions.

Source (quantum field theory, J(x))

Words: 69
Generating functional OurBigBook.com
An external source is a prescribed field coupled to a dynamical field or operator in the action, for example SJ​=S0​+∫Ji​(x)ϕi​(x)ddx. Functional derivatives of the generating functional with respect to J insert the corresponding fields into correlation functions. The source is varied to generate these insertions, rather than integrated over as a dynamical degree of freedom. Transforming it in the appropriate representation maintains an invariant source coupling when deriving a Ward identity.

Source differentiation inserts time-ordered field operators (Gr​=i−rδrZ/δJ(x1​)⋯δJ(xr​)∣J=0​)

Words: 41
Generating functional OurBigBook.com
A functional derivative of the source term in a Minkowski scalar field path integral inserts iϕ(x). Time-slicing identifies the resulting product with the time-ordered product of field operators. Dividing by the zero-source vacuum functional removes disconnected vacuum diagrams. The normalized formula has one factor 1/i for every insertion.

Normalized vacuum generating functional (Z[J]=Z[J]/Z[0])

Words: 207 Articles: 2
Generating functional OurBigBook.com
For a vacuum generating functional Z[J], normalization gives Z[J]=Z[J]/Z[0] and Z[0]=1. Functional derivatives of Z give normalized vacuum expectation values. The linked-cluster theorem shows that this ratio cancels Vacuum Feynman diagrams, while −ilogZ[J] gives connected correlators. Components attached to external insertions are not removed merely by the normalization.

Uniform-source vacuum functional and spacetime volume (F=Vd​μdf(λ,m2/μ2,h/μ3))

Words: 120
Normalized vacuum generating functional OurBigBook.com
A translation-invariant connected generating functional with a constant external source is extensive in spacetime volume Vd​. Its total logarithm is dimensionless, while its density has mass dimension d. Consequently its dimensionless representation at fixed physical volume must retain μdVd​. For a free massive scalar with source coupling μ−ϵ/2hϕ, completing the square gives F=Vd​μ−ϵh2/(2m2). This already disproves a literal rewriting of the full uniform-source logarithm using only λ,m2/μ2,h/μ3 at fixed volume. In infinite volume the total functional is generally infinite; use the density, a source of compact support, or an explicit volume regulator. After writing the density as μdf, its renormalization group equation has the engineering term +df. Ultraviolet subtraction alone does not establish infrared finiteness for a massless constant source.
